cells.tense: The first shape of a thing is held here while the pen is still in hand.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: One person could use a hand this week. Pick the help and see it all the way through — the move, the shift covered, the ride. When it's done, you're done.
cells.core:
When something is just starting, you can keep it whole while weight comes down on it. The load lands on what's true rather than what's quick, so what is beginning stays early without being hurried. None of this needs announcing for it to hold.

What is steady here moves outward. Pick one person and give them something real this week — a hand with the move, a shift covered, a ride — then let it be finished, no tab on it. Small enough to fit in a week and real enough to matter. The starting thing gets more room, and the help ends where it ends.

cells.tense: Something real is ready to begin, and the grip has gone tight before it has.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Put every feeling this thing brings on a single page. Keep all of them, cross nothing out, then close the page for the night.
cells.core:
You hold the first shape of something the way a person guards it before it can be touched: jaw set, the next move rehearsed, braced against a future the thing has not reached. The strength is real, and it is spending itself early. Nothing gets planted until it is certain.

Know the whole of what you feel before acting on it. Put every feeling about this on one page, all of it, nothing struck through, then stop for the night without fixing anything. Once all of it is named, the thing you hold stops carrying the unnamed part. The start is still there in the morning, and the feeling is complete.

cells.tense: The seed was set down at a door already behind, and the floor has gone quiet.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Get the whole thing out on one surface — papers, notes, numbers, whatever it lives in. Leave it spread out for a day and touch one piece.
cells.core:
Where weight gets borne, you are answering a room that already emptied. The load is here, and the strength that used to come from a new start has thinned out, so small loads land harder than they should. What you carry, you carry without the thing it was for.

Do not push harder into the weight; that part is running on fumes. Get the whole of it out on one surface, nothing in a drawer, and move a single piece. Leave it spread out for a day without deciding anything. Seeing all of it again is what brings strength back to the floor — you cannot hold what you cannot see.

cells.tense: Something is being made, and the room keeps the credit under another name.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: Some start got filed under timing and it was yours. Sit with the whole of it ten minutes — what you did, what landed right, what you carried — until nothing is left to look at. Write the date.
cells.core:
You have been the floor under a beginning and filed it as circumstance: the plan that came from nowhere, the call that landed right, the thing that got off the ground because you happened to be there. The making is credited to timing, and the start has no name on it. What you carry, you carry out of sight.

Look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see — what you did, what you carried, what landed where. Ten minutes; then the date on a page. That is not proof and not a plaque, just an accurate accounting. The part you did stops being a rumor once you have looked at all of it.
cells.sheetLine: The floor under that beginning is yours, filed under luck.

attempts.check: The draft leans on calling the person's grip on an idea 'steady' — the record shows the seed held, not the quality of their hold; drop the praise. A reader could reasonably say the holding is just what needs doing and not a capacity at all, which is why every ask is a small concrete act rather than a claim about what they are. If my read is wrong, the asks still stand: sharing one hour of help, naming an unfinished feeling, laying pieces on a table, or writing the first line still give something usable. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes the holding sound noble; the plain picture of the unspent seed does the work instead.
